readings: In `Products`, find each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices) and keep the types whose average is above the overall average price, if that average exists. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall average price, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types.
queries:
WITH type_averages AS (
  SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS type_avg_price
  FROM Products
  GROUP BY production_type_code
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS overall_avg_price
  FROM Products
),
kept AS (
  SELECT t.production_type_code, t.type_avg_price
  FROM type_averages AS t
  CROSS JOIN overall AS o
  WHERE t.type_avg_price > o.overall_avg_price
),
kept_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(type_avg_price) AS mean_kept_price
  FROM kept
)
SELECT
  AVG(k.type_avg_price) AS avg_type_price,
  AVG(k.type_avg_price - o.overall_avg_price) AS avg_above_overall,
  AVG(k.type_avg_price - m.mean_kept_price) AS avg_above_kept_mean
FROM kept AS k
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
CROSS JOIN kept_mean AS m
WHERE k.type_avg_price > m.mean_kept_price
